# SLC CPDLC Commands
.cpdlc .msg $aircraft CPDLC MESSAGE START... ISSUED $time FOR $aircraft | CDM ROUTE IS NOW ACTIVE FOR YOUR FLIGHT | NEW ROUTING: ***AMENDED*** $route ***AMENDED*** | CLEARANCE LIMIT: $arr | MAINTAIN 9,000 | EXPECT $cruise 10 MINUTES AFTER DEPARTURE | MAINTAIN 240 KTS UNTIL ADVISED | DEPARTURE FREQUENCY: $freq($1) | SQUAWK: $squawk | EXPECT RUNWAY $2 | CALL AT APPROPRIATE END OF RAMP FOR TAXI WITH ATIS | TO ACKNOWLEDGE AND ACCEPT, REPLY WITH 'W' (WILCO). IF UNABLE, REPLY 'U' (UNABLE) AND VERBALLY CONTACT CLEARANCE DELIVERY ...CPDLC MESSAGE END

.cpdlcs .msg $aircraft CPDLC MESSAGE START... ISSUED $time FOR $aircraft | CDM ROUTE IS NOW ACTIVE FOR YOUR FLIGHT | NEW ROUTING: ***AMENDED*** $route ***AMENDED*** | CLEARANCE LIMIT: $arr | MAINTAIN 9,000 | EXPECT $cruise 10 MINUTES AFTER DEPARTURE | DEPARTURE FREQUENCY: $freq($1) | SQUAWK: $squawk | EXPECTED RUNWAY $2 | CALL AT APPROPRIATE END OF RAMP FOR TAXI WITH ATIS | TO ACKNOWLEDGE AND ACCEPT, REPLY WITH 'W' (WILCO). IF UNABLE, REPLY 'U' (UNABLE) AND VERBALLY CONTACT CLEARANCE DELIVERY ...CPDLC MESSAGE END

.cpdlcg .msg $aircraft CPDLC MESSAGE START... ISSUED $time FOR $aircraft | CDM ROUTE IS NOW ACTIVE FOR YOUR FLIGHT | NEW ROUTING: ***AMENDED*** $route ***AMENDED*** | CLEARANCE LIMIT: $arr | MAINTAIN 9,000 | EXPECT $cruise 10 MINUTES AFTER DEPARTURE | MAINTAIN 240 KTS UNTIL ADVISED | DEPARTURE FREQUENCY: $freq($1) | SQUAWK: $squawk | EXPECTED RUNWAY $2 | GATE HOLD IN EFFECT. CONTACT CLEARANCE FOR EDCT | TO ACKNOWLEDGE AND ACCEPT, REPLY WITH 'W' (WILCO). IF UNABLE, REPLY 'U' (UNABLE) AND VERBALLY CONTACT CLEARANCE DELIVERY ...CPDLC MESSAGE END

.cpdlcsg .msg $aircraft CPDLC MESSAGE START... ISSUED $time FOR $aircraft | CDM ROUTE IS NOW ACTIVE FOR YOUR FLIGHT | NEW ROUTING: ***AMENDED*** $route ***AMENDED*** | CLEARANCE LIMIT: $arr | MAINTAIN 9,000 | EXPECT $cruise 10 MINUTES AFTER DEPARTURE | DEPARTURE FREQUENCY: $freq($1) | SQUAWK: $squawk | EXPECTED RUNWAY $2 | GATE HOLD IN EFFECT. # MISC

.EDCT .MSG $aircraft *** ADVISORY *** This route is under a Traffic Management Delay Program from VATUSA. Your assigned departure (takeoff) time is $1. Time now $time. Monitor DEL freq for possible amendments prior to calling GND for taxi. Contact GND 5-7min prior to your departure time, ready for taxi. Advise ATC if unable to meet assigned time or with questions. *** END ***

.MAD .MSG $aircraft *** We understand your frustration with this time restriction. However, the field you are flying to can only support so many arrivals and departures within a certain time and maintain appropriate separation from other aircraft. To help mitigate traffic congestion, VATUSA is establishing more realistic delay programs like this. More specific questions should be directed to VATUSA86 via private message in your pilot client.

# "Trouble Pilot"
.PRC .MSG ZLC_ISR With all due respect, it appears that there is a significant amount of knowledge that is still required on your part to complete flights like this on the network per the VATSIM Expectations and Requirements for Pilots. Please navigate to the VATSIM Pilot Resource Center site and start there.
.TIPS .msg ZLC_ISR There has been 1 or more encounters with you that would make us think you might benefit from some resources we have posted on our site to help pilots with misc procedures. It is our Tips for Pilots section. Take a look at it sometime. Have a great day! zlcartcc.org
.WHATRWY .MSG ZLC_ISR After you get your clearance, it is standard for pilots to program their main route and leave off the SID portion in the FMS because they usually do not get their RWY assignment until they notify the ATC of their position on the field and request taxi. Then during taxi, the pilot then programs the rest of the SID portion. So you will get that information when you call for taxi.
.TWRFREQ .MSG ZLC_ISR Upon reaching the departure runway and ready to request takeoff, you are expected to change to the appropriate frequency for Tower on your own, without being told to do so. Reference the Federal Aviation Administration Aeronautical Information Manual 4-3-14.a https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/publications/atpubs/aim_html/chap4_section_3.html#$paragraph4-3-14

# 'Bad Pilot set by Josh Glottman 11/2025
.BADI .msg INFO [NO FPL] PLAN, PLANN, PLANC, PLANM. [BAD SPAWN] BADRWY, BADTWY, BADPUSH. [MOV WO PMSN] BADTAXI, BADHS, BADTR, BADTWR, BADAIR, BADA. [FPL ISSUES] BADCALL, BADCALLF, BADREG, BADEQ, BADTYPE, BADTYPE2, BADRTE, BADRUN. [DEP ISSUES] BADC, BADC2, BADCA, BADPR, BADPRC, BADIND, BADTO, BADACC, BADRT. [IDENT ISSUES] BADFL, BADFLA, BADALC, BADCI, BADCI2, BADVFR. [ALT DEV] BADALT, BADALP, BADALD, BADDV. [LATERAL DEV] BADLAT, BADLAT2, BADHD, BADVEC, BADFLY, BADSPD, BADSPP, BAD250, BADHOLD. [MISC] BADSD, BADRC, BADLIS, BADRA, BADRD, BADEST, BADSR, BADWIND, BADSEC, BADMSFS, BADMIC. [WALL CTL] WALLC, WALLCH, WALLHM. [WALL AFK] WALLAFK, WALLAFKN, WALLAFKD, WALLAFKX, WALLU, WALLT. [CHARTS] CHARTD, CHARTA, CHARTDD, CHARTAA.

#    NO FPL    #
.PLAN .msg $aircraft Hello, you currently do not have a flight plan on file. Please disconnect, refile your flight plan, then reconnect. Upon refiling, please contact me on $freq(). Thank you!
.PLANN .msg $aircraft Hello, you currently do not have a flight plan on file. Please disconnect, refile your flight plan, then reconnect. Thank you!
.PLANC .msg $aircraft Hello, you currently do not have a flight plan on file. Please disconnect, refile your flight plan, then reconnect. Be sure to double check that the callsign for the flightplan is $aircraft. Thank you!

#  BAD SPAWN   #
.BADRWY .msg $aircraft Hello, you have started up on an active runway, please exit immediately and relocate your aircraft to the nearest ramp. Do not slew or taxi. Thank you! :D
.BADTWY .msg $aircraft Hello, you have started up on an active taxiway, please relocate your aircraft to the nearest ramp immediately. Do not slew or taxi. Thank you! :D
.BADPUSH .msg $aircraft Hello, please contact ATC in the future prior to pushing back onto a controlled taxiway. Thank you! :D

# MOV WO PMSN  #
.BADTAXI .msg $aircraft Hello, the airport you are located at is currently towered and I am providing top-down services there at this time. Please hold position and contact me on $freq() immediately. In the future, please check for online ATC - https://map.vatsim.net. Thank you! :D
.BADHS .msg $aircraft Hello, it appears you have entered a runway or taxiway that you were instructed to hold short of and/or had no permission to enter. You may never enter or cross a runway without explicit instructions. If you are told to hold short of a runway or taxiway, you may not enter the specified hold short runway/taxiway until you have received explicit permission to do so. In the future, pay close attention to hold short and explicit runway crossing instructions; failing to do so may cause substantial delays for yourself and others. Thank you! :D
.BADTR .msg $aircraft Hello, it appears that you have taxied via the wrong taxiways and/or disregarded a hold short instruction. In the future, verify and validate your taxi instructions thoroughly as errors while taxiing may result in delays for yourself and others. Thank you! :D
.BADTWR .msg $aircraft Hello, you have just departed a towered airport without contacting ATC. Please contact me on $freq() immediately. In the future, you must check for online ATC - https://map.vatsim.net. Thank you! :D
.BADAIR .msg $aircraft Hello, the airspace you are in is controlled and you have entered it without appropriate permission. Please contact me on $freq() immediately and exit the airspace. In the future, please check for online ATC - https://map.vatsim.net. Additionally familiarize yourself with the airspace you are flying in - https://skyvector.com. Thank you! :D
.BADA .msg $aircraft Hello, you have entered the lateral and vertical boundaries of my airspace. Please contact me on $freq() as soon as practical. You can approximate your position relative to my airspace by visiting https://map.vatsim.net. In the future, please contact me a few minutes prior to airspace entry. Thank you! :D

#  FPL ISSUES  #
.BADCALL .msg $aircraft Hello, the callsign $aircraft is not a valid callsign for the airline you are trying to fly. The correct callsign for this flight is $uc($1). Please note, some air traffic controllers will identify you by the wrong callsign and you will display incorrectly for all pilots online. In the future, it is recommended that you login with the correct callsign for your airline. Thank you! :D
.BADCALLF .msg $aircraft Hello, the callsign $aircraft, while not prohibited, is not typically how airline callsigns are formatted for U.S. air carriers. Most U.S. air carrier callsigns are comprised of 1-4 digits with no additional letters (unless there is a conflicting flight with the same callsign). No need to change your callsign at this time, just something to consider when flying again in the U.S. again in the future. Thanks and have a nice flight! :D
.BADREG .msg $aircraft Hello, the registration $aircraft is not a valid registration for an aircraft registered in the United States. Aircraft registrations in the U.S. start with an "N" and are comprised of 1-5 additional characters, with only the last two characters possibly being letters. The first number cannot be a "0" and the letters "I" and "O" are not valid (as they can be easily confused with numbers). Here are a few valid registrations for example: N123AB, N1234A, N12345, N12AB, N123A, N1234, N1AB, N12A, N123, N1A, N12, N1. In the future, it is recommended that you login with a valid U.S. registration if you plan on flying with a N-registered aircraft. Thank you! :D
.BADEQ .msg $aircraft Hello, it appears your filed flight plan may include an invalid ICAO equipment information (the "Equipment" section on the VATSIM flight plan form). This information is important to providing us with details about your aircraft's navigation and transponder capabilities. Please refer to this reference guide when filing in the future: https://support.foreflight.com/hc/en-us/articles/360049193173-ICAO-Equipment-and-PBN-Guide. Thank you! :D
.BADTYPE .msg $aircraft Hello, the correct aircraft type for the plane you are flying is "$uc($1)". Please make sure you file and connect with the correct aircraft type in the future. Thank you! :D
.BADTYPE2 .msg $aircraft Hello, it appears that you may have filed and/or connected with an invalid aircraft type ($type($aircraft)). The correct aircraft type for the plane you are flying can be found here: https://www.icao.int/publications/DOC8643/Pages/Search.aspx. Thank you! :D
.BADRTE .msg $aircraft Hello, the route you filed is not optimal and/or does not contain a SID/STAR. Real-world routes between $dep and $arr can (usually) be found here: https://www.flightaware.com/analysis/route.rvt?origin=$dep&destination=$arr. Thank you! :D
.BADRUN .msg $aircraft Hello, in the future, please do not include airports, runways, and/or approaches in the route section of your flightplan. The route section should only include your SID, enroute routing, and STAR. Thank you! :D

#  DEP ISSUES  #
.BADC .msg $aircraft Hello, at $dep, it is required that you operate your transponder in altitude reporting mode (Mode C) and squawk your assigned transponder code ($squawk) prior to moving on airport surfaces. In the future, make sure both transponder items are set prior to requesting pushback or taxi instructions. Thank you! :D
.BADC2 .msg $aircraft Hello, at $arr, it is required that you operate your transponder in altitude reporting mode (Mode C) while moving on airport surfaces. In the future, do not squawk standby until the aircraft has stopped in a non-movement area. Thank you! :D
.BADCA .msg $aircraft Hello, it is required that you operate your transponder in altitude reporting mode (Mode C) while airborne while on an IFR flightplan and/or within 30 NM of a Class B airport. Thank you! :D
.BADPR .msg $aircraft Hello, at most airports in the U.S., it is not required to request pushback if you are pushing into a ramp or other non-movement area. Unless charts, the ATIS, or your PDC states otherwise, please do not request pushback unless you need to push into a taxiway. Thank you! :D
.BADPRC .msg $aircraft Hello, at most airports in the U.S., it is not required to request pushback if you are pushing into a ramp or other non-movement area. Unless charts, the ATIS, or your PDC states otherwise, please do not request pushback unless you need to push into a taxiway. Additionally, please squawk normal (Mode C) prior to moving on airport surfaces. Thank you! :D
.BADIND .msg $aircraft Hello, in the future, unless you are told to depart at an intersection or explicitly request it, please taxi to use the full length of your assigned runway. Taxiing to an intersection without prior coordination/approval can result in delays in your departure. Thank you! :D
.BADTO .msg $aircraft Hello, during your recent takeoff, it appeared that you spent a long amount of time sitting on the runway without moving. In the future, please begin your takeoff immediately after receiving your takeoff clearance or inform ATC that you require additional time to setup. Delaying your takeoff roll can result in go arounds, rejected takeoffs, and losses of separation. Thank you! :D
.BADACC .msg $aircraft Hello, the departure procedure you are flying requires that you accelerate to 250 knots as soon as practical. In the future, please be mindful of restrictions like this and accelerate to 250 knots sooner after departure (rather than maintaining a slower airspeed during your climb). Thank you! :D
.BADRT .msg $aircraft Hello, during your recent takeoff, you did not verify first waypoint on your SID during your takeoff clearance. When issued an instruction similar to "RNAV CSALT...", you must readback that portion of your takeoff clearance and verify that the correct waypoint, SID, and runway are selected in your FMS. If the takeoff clearance does not match the selected procedure, refuse the takeoff clearance until the discrepancy is resolved. Thank you! :D

# IDENT ISSUES #
.BADFL .msg $aircraft Hello, the term "flight level" only refers to altitudes at or above 18,000 feet in the U.S. and indicates that the aircraft is using a standard (29.92) altimeter setting. Thank you! :D
.BADFLA .msg $aircraft Hello, the term "flight level" should be used to refer to altitudes at or above 18,000 feet in the U.S. and indicates that the aircraft is using a standard (29.92) altimeter setting. Thank you! :D
.BADALC .msg $aircraft Hello, in the future, please check in with your current altitude or flight level on initial contact with all controllers. It helps us verify that the Mode C function of your transponder is reporting correctly. Although it is not necessary in every scenario, ATC is often required to ask for your altitude if you don't provide it. (If you did check in with your altitude on initial contact, and I missed it - please disregard this message). Thank you! :D
.BADCI .msg $aircraft Hello, in the future, please do not check in with only your callsign as this provides no useful information and wastes valuable time on frequency. On initial contact, state your callsign and current altitude or flight level (if you have an additional request, state that as well). Thank you! :D
.BADCI2 .msg $aircraft Hello, in the future, please do not check in with only your callsign as this provides no useful information and wastes valuable time on frequency. On initial contact, state your callsign and request. Thank you! :D
.BADVFR .msg $aircraft Hello, as a VFR aircraft, I am unable to see any information about your aircraft or any flight plan you file (VFR flight plans are for search and rescue purposes only in the U.S.). For that reason, it is greatly appreciated if you check in with your full callsign, destination, and aircraft type when making a VFR request. For example, "N123AB, request flight following to Half Moon Bay (HAF) at 4500, Cessna 172 (C172)." Please let me know if you have any questions. Thank you! :D

#   ALT DEV    #
.BADALT .msg $aircraft Hello, it appears you did not comply with a published altitude restriction on your SID/STAR. In the future, please ensure you comply with all altitude and speed restrictions unless explicitly told otherwise. The restrictions exist to protect you from other aircraft departing from and arriving to the airspace you are currently flying in. Thank you! :D
.BADALP .msg $aircraft Hello, you did not comply with the published/assigned initial altitude on your departure procedure. It is extremely important that you maintain your initial altitude as it protects you from other departing and arriving aircraft. If your clearance included an instruction to "climb via SID", you must comply with all published altitudes on the SID including the TOP ALTITUDE. You will (almost) never be permitted to climb to your cruise altitude initially. Thank you! :D
.BADALD .msg $aircraft Hello, it appears you may have deviated from your assigned altitude. In the future, please ensure you do not climb above/descend below your assigned altitude without permission. Thank you! :D
.BADDV .msg $aircraft Hello, when issued a "descend via" instruction, the descent occurs at the pilot's discretion to comply with all published altitudes and speeds on the arrival (you can simply report leaving your cruising altitude without requesting permission). Thank you! :D

# LATERAL DEV  #
.BADLAT .msg $aircraft Hello, it appears that you may have deviated from the lateral course of your filed/assigned route. If you are flying a procedure (SID/STAR/IAP), it is helpful to cross-reference your planned route with the procedure's chart to ensure compliance. Please rejoin your filed/assigned route immediately in order to avoid substantial delays. Thank you! :D
.BADLAT2 .msg $aircraft Hello, it appears you have incorrectly programmed your filed STAR and are not following its route correctly. Please immediately reprogram the STAR with the correct transition/routing. You have likely deleted many waypoints that are required to comply with the routing of the STAR. Failure to fix your routing immediately will result in substantial delays. In the future, you must fly and program your arrival procedure correctly. Thank you! :D
.BADHD .msg $aircraft Hello, it appears you have deviated from your assigned heading. In the future, please ensure you do not deviate from your assigned heading without permission. Thank you! :D
.BADVEC .msg $aircraft Hello, it appears you may have deleted/not flown a vector segment on the SID/STAR you are currently flying. In the future, please ensure you comply with the vector segment. The segment exists to protect you from other aircraft departing from and arriving to the airspace you are currently flying in. Thank you! :D
.BADFLY .msg $aircraft Hello, it appears that you are struggling to control your aircraft and/or comply with assigned instructions. It is highly recommended that you practice flying your aircraft offline to familiarize yourself with its systems and controls prior to flying online. Failure to comply with ATC instructions and/or maintain positive control of your aircraft may result in substantial delays in the future. Thank you! :D
.BADSPD .msg $aircraft Hello, it appears that you have slowed down to your approach speed particularly early. While not mandatory (unless explicitly given a speed restriction), it is recommended that you maintain around 210 knots until a 10 NM final. This helps reduce the amount of time you spend on your approach and generally makes the traffic flow more efficiently. Thank you! :D
.BADSPP .msg $aircraft Hello, pilots are required to maintain the last published speed on a STAR until ATC assigns a new speed, issues a vector, assigns a direct route, or issues an approach clearance. In the future, please maintain the last published speed on the STAR until one of those conditions occurs. Thank you! :D
.BAD250 .msg $aircraft Hello, it appears that you may have exceed 250 knots (indicated airspeed) while operating below 10,000 feet MSL. In the future, ensure your aircraft remains below 250 knots while operating below 10,000 feet (unless the minimum safe airspeed for your aircraft is greater than 250 knots). Thank you! :D
.BADHOLD .msg $aircraft Hello, you were recently instructed to fly a hold at a certain waypoint. You have incorrectly flown your assigned hold. It is extremely important that you understand how to fly holding procedures in your aircraft. Holds are usually issued as a method to delay airborne traffic during high volume operations, changes in airport flow direction, or severe weather. If you cannot correctly fly a hold during these situations, it adds significant additional workload for the controller. Prior to flying online, you should familiarize yourself with and practice correctly flying hold entries and holding patterns in any aircraft you intend on flying. Here is a video that may be helpful in understanding holds: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vXLcIScV_xY. Thank you! :D

#     MISC     #
.BADSD .msg $aircraft Hello, pilots should exit the runway without delay at the first available taxiway (unless instructed otherwise by ATC). In the future, please do not stop on the runway or taxi slowly while exiting the runway. (An aircraft is considered clear of the runway when all parts of the aircraft are past the runway edge). Thank you! :D
.BADRC .msg $aircraft Hello, please refrain from requesting a radio check unless absolutely necessary as it wastes valuable frequency time. First, listen to the frequency and see if you can hear the controller or nearby pilots. Next, contact the controller with your request. If you don't receive a response after a few calls and adequate time, you may be experiencing a technical issue. If your radio is truly bad, the controller will let you know. For troubleshooting, visit https://vpilot.rosscarlson.dev/Documentation (vPilot) or https://docs.xpilot-project.org/docs (xPilot). Thank you! :D
.BADLIS .msg $aircraft Hello, it appears you are not able to hear my transmissions and/or not paying attention to the frequency as I have issued a few instructions without receiving your response in a timely manner. Please listen to the frequency closely to ensure any instructions are not missed. If you are struggling to hear me, please let me know and I will use text. Failure to respond to additional instructions may result in substantial delays. Thank you! :D
.BADRA .msg $aircraft Hello, as an enroute controller, I am unable to issue runway assignments at most airports. If there is no approach controller online, I am able to issue a runway assignment once you are in the terminal area (usually 50-75 NM away from the airport). This should still leave a reasonable amount of time to plan/configure your FMS. Thank you! :D
.BADRD .msg $aircraft Hello, please do not request a departure runway assignment as it may not be determined until taxi instructions are issued. If an ATIS online, it may contain information about the current active departure runway(s). Thank you! :D
.BADEST .msg $aircraft Hello, it is not required to report established on the localizer or final approach course in the U.S. while in a radar environment. In the future, please do not report established as it wastes valuable frequency time. If you are on short final without a landing clearance, feel free to inquire with ATC. Thank you! :D
.BADSR .msg $aircraft Hello, it appears you are using an increased simulation rate. Please return to a normal simulation rate when able. Thank you! :D
.BADWIND .msg $aircraft Hello, it appears your simulator's modeled winds may be incorrect (as other pilots near you assigned similar speeds are going much slower/faster than you). Please ensure you are using real world weather and verify that your internet connection is stable. Thank you! :D
.BADSEC .msg $aircraft Hello, for your awareness, at times we may utilize multiple frequencies that are not directly visible to your pilot client. Please ask if you believe you heard a frequency incorrectly, but generally do not worry if you are switched to a frequency that isn't on your controller list (there's no controller list real world). Thanks and have a nice flight! :D
.BADMSFS .msg $aircraft Hello, it appears your frequency may have automatically switched due to settings in MSFS. Please avoid using "Career Mode" or "AI Radio Communications (ATC)" while connected to the network as they cause automated frequency changes to occur. Thank you! :D
.BADMIC .msg $aircraft Hello, it appears that your microphone volume is too loud/quiet and/or the sound quality is very bad. Please re-calibrate your microphone and/or adjust the microphone volume level. For troubleshooting,  https://vpilot.rosscarlson.dev/Documentation (vPilot) or https://docs.xpilot-project.org/docs (xPilot). Thank you! :D

#   WALL CTL   #
.WALLC .wallop $aircraft - pilot is unable to maintain positive control of their aircraft and is not able to maintain altitude, heading, and/or speed.
.WALLCH .wallop $aircraft - pilot does not have charts on board and is generally unprepared to fly the SID, STAR, and/or IAP that they filed/were assigned.
.WALLHM .wallop $aircraft - hot mic on frequency. Need immediate assistance!

#   WALL AFK   #
.WALLAFK .wallop $aircraft - pilot is AFK, first contactme sent at $1Z.
.WALLAFKN .wallop $aircraft - pilot is AFK, first contactme sent at $1Z. Not urgent, fine to give the pilot another $2 minutes to respond.
.WALLAFKD .wallop $aircraft - pilot is AFK, first contactme sent at $1Z. Pilot currently is (or will soon be) missing their top of descent into $arr.
.WALLAFKX .wallop $aircraft - pilot is AFK, first contactme sent at $1Z. Pilot will be a conflict with other aircraft shortly.
.WALLU .wallop $aircraft - pilot not responding to contactmes and will be a conflict with other aircraft shortly.
.WALLT .wallop $aircraft - pilot not responding to contactmes and taxiing and/or taking off at a towered airport without permission.

# Military
.OVERHEAD .MSG ZLC_ISR Overhead_Manuever_Phraseology*** WIND ### @ ##. PATTERN ALTITUDE ###. (Right/Left) TURNS. REPORT INITIAL RUNWAY ##. ____ [Initial Report] BREAK AT (numbers/midfield/departure end). REPORT BREAK. ____ [Break Report] CHECK GEAR DOWN. RWY ## CLEARED TO LAND.
.MILCT .MSG ZLC_ISR Military Takeoff Clearance*** Military aircraft (except Cargo and Transport types), WIND---@-- RWY-- CLEARED FOR TAKEOFF
.MILCL .MSG ZLC_ISR Wind $wind($arr). Check Wheels Down. RWY ## Cleared to Land.

# Released for Departure (Uncontrolled Field)
.RFD .MSG ZLC_ISR *** $aircraft Released for departure. Clearance void if not off by $ftime(10). If not off by $ftime(10), advise $radioname() on $freq() not later than $ftime(15) of intentions. Time now- $time. Frequency change approved.

# Holding instructions
.HOLDING .MSG ZLC_ISR *** HOLD (direction) OF (waypoint). ON THE (radial, course, bearing, track, azimuth, airway, or route).(leg length of hold if applicable).(state Left Turns, if right turns are not to be assumed).MAINTAIN (altitude).EXPECT FURTHER CLEARANCE (time).

# IFR Procedures Phraseology Help
.OTP .MSG ZLC_ISR *** CLIMB TO AND REPORT REACHING VFR ON TOP, TOPS REPORTED (altitude, if none "NO TOPS REPORTED"), IF NOT ON TOP AT (altitude), MAINTAIN (altitude), AND ADVISE. MAINTAIN VFR ON TOP.

# 3LD TELEPHONY (CUSTOM)

.idCXA .MSG ZLC_ISR *** 3LD: CXA ___ TELEPHONY: XIAMEN AIR (Virtual: Canadian Express)
.idXIAMENAIR .MSG ZLC_ISR *** 3LD: CXA ___ TELEPHONY: XIAMEN AIR (Virtual: Canadian Express)
.idCanadianExpress .MSG ZLC_ISR *** 3LD: CXA ___ TELEPHONY: XIAMEN AIR (Virtual: Canadian Express)

.idBVI .MSG ZLC_ISR *** 3LD: BVI ___ TELEPHONY: DRAKE (Virtual: Vision Jet [Visually impaired])

#                        TEXT TO PILOTS

# General
.tnew .msg $aircraft Hello, it appears you may be new to the network. First of all - welcome to VATSIM! It may be tempting to jump right ahead and fly, but I would suggest you read through some documents first, in order to prepare yourself for what you may encounter. First of all - you should read the VATSIM tutorials at vats.im/prc. Here you can find everything you need. Second of all, you should read through the VATSIM Code of Conduct (vats.im/coc), especially sections A and B, in order to not get in trouble for something you didn't know. Let me know if you have any other questions, thanks for flying today!
.tsq Squawk $squawk
.tcon Contact $radioname($1) on $freq($1).
.tmon Monitor $radioname($1) on $freq($1).
.tCLOSING  ****NOTAM $radioname() is closing in $1 minutes. ****
.tCLOSED  ****NOTAM $radioname() closed at $time Zulu. ****
.tprc With all due respect, it appears that there is a significant amount of knowledge that is still required on your part to complete flights like this on the network per the VATSIM Expectations and Requirements for Pilots. Please navigate to the VATSIM Pilot Resource Center site and start there.
.THOTMIC ATTENTION ALL AIRCRAFT: Someone is continuing to press the MIC button. Please check your connections and resolve this issue as it is disrupting communications on this frequency.
.TTIPS There has been 1 or more encounters with you that would make us think you might benefit from some resources we have posted on our site to help pilots with misc procedures. It is our Tips for Pilots section. Take a look at it sometime. Have a great day! zlcartcc.org
.TWHATRWY After you get your clearance, it is standard for pilots to program their main route and leave off the SID portion in the FMS because they usually do not get their RWY assignment until they notify the ATC of their position on the field and request taxi. Then during taxi, the pilot then programs the rest of the SID portion. So you will get that information when you call for taxi.
.TTWRFREQ .msg $aircraft Upon reaching the departure runway and ready to request takeoff, you are expected to change to the appropriate frequency for Tower on your own, without being told to do so. Reference the Federal Aviation Administration Aeronautical Information Manual 4-3-14.a https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/publications/atpubs/aim_html/chap4_section_3.html#$paragraph4-3-14
#.TEQUIP .msg $aircraft What is your equipment suffix code? ***I am NOT asking for your Aircraft Code: "$type($aircraft)"*** If you need help, visit this website: https://equipment-suffix.febuddy.com/
.TPDC? The message you got via private message is a way of simulating a real world system called Controller Pilot Data Link Communications (CPDLC). At certain airports in the real world, your departure clearance is provided via this system without the need for any voice communications. If you don't have any questions concerning the clearance, just prepare your aircraft with that information and report to Ground Control when ready for taxi, squawking your assigned code.
.TNnumber .msg $aircraft Your callsign seems to be not valid. This link assists you format your callsign per USA regulation. Thank you for the help! https://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/aircraft_certification/aircraft_registry/forming_nnumber/

# Voice/Receive Only/Text COMMUNICATIONS CAPABILITIES
# "Communication capabilities… Ideally, we’d like you to use Full Voice (V), where you both transmit and receive by voice—this makes our job much 
# easier. If Full Voice isn’t possible, Receiving (R) by voice and replying via text is the next best option. The least preferred method is using 
# Full Text (T) where you both transmit and receive via text, this is discouraged as this makes our job significantly more difficult. 
# Please let me know what your maximum communication capability is… V, R, or T?"

.Tvrt? .msg $aircraft Communication capabilities… Ideally, we’d like you to use Full Voice (V), where you both transmit and receive by voice—this makes our job much easier. If Full Voice isn’t possible, Receiving (R) by voice and replying via text is the next best option. The least preferred method is using Full Text (T) where you both transmit and receive via text, this is discouraged as this makes our job significantly more difficult. Please let me know what your maximum communication capability is… V, R, or T?

# Clearance Delivery
.trbc Read Back Correct.

# General CRAFT
.TCRAFTU Cleared to $arr via $route. Departure frequency is with UNICOM 122.800, squawk $squawk
.TCRAFT Cleared to $arr. Fly heading $1 expect radar vectors on course $route. Maint $2. Departure frequency $freq($3), squawk $squawk
.TNOPDC .msg $aircraft ***ADVISORY*** A Pre-Departure Clearance (PDC) was unable to be sent to you due to a lack of sufficient information in your flight plan. Please contact $radioname($1) on $freq($1) for your clearance delivery.

# Ground
.trtv Runway $uc($1), taxi via $2 $3
.ttpv Taxi to parking via $1 $2

# Tower
.tcl Runway $uc($1), Wind $winds, cleared to land.
.tct Runway $uc($1), Wind $winds, cleared for takeoff.

# Radar-General
.tsqi squawk $squawk and ident
.trc Radar Contact
.tfh Fly heading $1
.ttl Turn left heading $1
.ttr Turn right heading $1
.trst Radar Services Terminated
.tcm Climb and maintain $1
.tdm Descend and maintain $1

# Departure
.thfr Hold for release.
.trfd Released for departure. Clearance void if not off by $ftime(10). If not off by $ftime(10), advise $radioname() on $freq() not later than $ftime(15) of intentions. Time now- $time Zulu. Frequency change approved.

# Approach
.tptac $dist($1) miles from $uc($1), Fly heading $2. Maintain $3 until established on the localizer. Cleared $4 runway $5 approach.
.tptacils $dist($1) miles from $uc($1), Fly heading $2. Maintain $3 until established on the localizer. Cleared ILS runway $4 approach.
.trfis Airport is at your $oclock($arr), $dist($arr) miles, report in sight
.tcva Cleared visual runway $1 approach.

# En-Route
.trcdb Radar Contact $dist($1) miles $bear($1) of $uc($1)
.tlma Leaving my airspace, radar service terminated, frequency change approved.
